title: Codex integration owner cannot delete path-checked folders in its own project's .logs/.evidence/target/.worktrees: recursive delete refused 'blocked by policy' before execution
outcome: Codex integration owner cannot delete path-checked folders in its own project's .logs/.evidence/target/.worktrees: recursive delete refused 'blocked by policy' before execution
acceptance: The original reported refusals are recorded with verbatim tool results and relevant command/runtime policy evidence; the rejecting layer and mechanism are identified, or the missing discriminator is explicitly documented without claiming an unproved cause.

An authenticated project-bound integration owner has a supported bounded cleanup operation for disposable descendants of its own project's .logs, .evidence, target and .worktrees. It performs an authorized disposable-fixture cleanup and records actual outcome without requiring another agent to execute the deletion. Any registered worktree root or descendant is refused with a typed reason directing the caller to the existing git worktree remove without --force route.

The operation refuses other-project/outside-root/root-directory/.git/protected-build targets, traversal and link/reparse escapes, registered worktree roots and descendants, and host-known active/frozen/gated paths. Static preflight refusals leave their targets unchanged; concurrent mutation or post-start failure is reported honestly as potentially partial, while deletion never follows a link outside the authorized root. The caller's workRefs and reason are recorded verbatim; retention decisions remain governed by the coordinator's and integration owner's existing cleanup rule, without claiming machine-checked tracker retention in v1. Tests cover allowed cleanup, enforced boundaries and Windows junction/race behavior.

The operation preserves existing Codex sandbox/approval settings and normal shell-denial behavior; any new delete-authority wording/grant has the repository-required exact-wording concurrence and Greg authorization before it is enabled/landed, with standard review and gate evidence on the final input.

blockers.detail: Parked by Fable1432: unresolved path-authorization proof, authenticated destructive caller transport/operator-only grant provisioning, shared exclusion owner integration, and coordination schema/reader compatibility prerequisites make v1 cost exceed current P2 value. Coordinator path-checked cleanup workaround remains supported. Resume only on coordinator reprioritization with these prerequisites resolved; no implementation authority.
